patch_description:
The original program failed because its recursive row/column reordering machinery was fundamentally broken relative to the actual objective and API: it returned an empty `column_orderings` list, mixed row values across columns via `result_df.loc[i] = ...` with `as_completed` (nondeterministic row assignment), mutated/dropped columns, fabricated an `original_index` column, and its `find_max_group_value`/`reorder_columns_for_value` used `hasattr`/`getattr` on namedtuples that crashed on duplicate/space-containing column names (visible in stdout: columns like `review/profileName`, `movieinfo_rottentomatoeslink_movietitle`). The whole approach optimized squared field lengths and adjacent-row grouping, which does not match the serial character-Trie reuse objective.

The fix replaces the entire editable block with a clean, correct implementation: it serializes cells (missing -> "") exactly as the evaluator does, builds a small bounded set of candidate global column orderings (original order; frequency-ranked order scoring each column by sum(len(v)*count*(count-1)); a length-weighted variant), scores each candidate with the exact ideal Trie reuse (sum of adjacent LCPs of the sorted serialized rows, using fast C-speed slice comparisons), and returns the best. `col_merge` groups are kept contiguous. All cells, rows, and columns are preserved; a single global column order is applied so the returned DataFrame is exactly consistent with `column_orderings` (one ordering per row). Row order and values are untouched, guaranteeing validation passes.
